bull_bear.body: Prioritizing strategic capex: compressors, refrigerants, WM expansion; maintaining discipline on returns; no dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on cash flow generation and working capital normalization in FY27.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: FX volatility (rupee at INR95.5 vs budgeted INR94); El Nino uncertainty impacting AC season; labor shortages due to fuel cost and new Labour Code; global geopolitical risks (Gulf conflict) disrupting LPG supply; margin recovery dependent on sustained price pass-through and stable exchange rates.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledged severe FY26 headwinds but emphasized structural tailwinds (outsourcing trend, low AC penetration, energy transition); confident in new capacity execution and cost discipline; avoided giving FY27 guidance but signaled normalization and recovery.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: LPG crisis caused 2-week shutdown in March, leading to INR300cr revenue loss; truck shortage stranded INR120cr of finished goods; forex loss of INR25.82cr in Q4 was largely due to mark-to-market on unhedged LCs at INR94.8; compressor facility requires no external approvals; 60% localization in compressors; inventory normalized from INR1,600cr (Mar) to target <INR900cr by June 2026.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Cash & Bank Balances stood at INR 491.3 crores at the end of 1QFY27, and the company is again in a net cash position."
- Balance sheet at 30th Jun'26 shows Gross Debt 417.4, Cash & Bank Balance 491.3 and Net Debt (73.9) INR crores, versus Net Debt of 110.3 at 31st Mar'26 (where Net Debt/Equity is shown as 0.0 and Net Debt/EBITDA as 0.3); Net Debt/Equity and Net Debt/EBITDA are shown as "NA" for both June dates.
- Returns on the deck's own definitions stepped down: RoCE (TTM) 26.0% at 30th Jun'25 to 13.4% at 30th Jun'26 (13.3% at 31st Mar'26), and RoE (TTM) 13.4% to 6.7% (6.6% at 31st Mar'26).
- Capital-allocation philosophy framed as "Improving profitability and higher cash-flows, will lead to better capital efficiency and stronger balance sheet" and "Reinvesting to improve strategic capabilities to reap future benefits"; no dividend or buyback is mentioned.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- integration: room-AC components made in-house — evidence: at the Ahmednagar and Bhiwadi AC facilities 'plastic components, sheet metal components, cross flow fans, heat exchangers, copper tubing and controllers are all produced in-house' — against it: the rotary compressor is not yet in-house; the Supa compressor project is still in progress
- scale: room-AC manufacturing capacity — evidence: 4.5 million units RAC annual manufacturing capacity; company states it is the largest manufacturer of room AC CBUs in India — against it: the report attributes the FY 2025-26 operating-profit decline to negative operating leverage and lower capacity utilisation in the Room AC business
- technology: in-house ODM design platforms and tooling — evidence: tooling division established 2016; four ODM platforms for air conditioners launched in 2022 and a new ODM washing machine platform launched later
- integration: forward integration into refrigerators from its existing refrigerator component-kit supply — evidence: Sri City refrigerator facility under construction with 1.2 million units initial annual capacity planned [planned]
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on the seasonal room-AC business — Room air conditioners anchor the product business. In FY2025-26 early rains in May 2025 and the August 2025 GST cut announcement postponed demand, and the business suffered negative operating leverage and lower capacity utilisation, which management blames for the fall in operating profit.
- Working-capital strain from inventory and receivables — Inventory and debtors rose faster than sales as high channel inventory slowed primary sales and collections in the RAC forward channel were slow. This raised bank-limit usage and interest costs and weakened the current and debt-equity ratios.
- Supply chain and raw-material price volatility — Disruptions in component availability or logistics, or swings in raw-material prices, can hit production and costs. The report cites gas supply disruption in 4Q FY2026 linked to the Iran war, and elevated raw-material prices. Mitigation: localisation, backward integration, supplier diversification.
- Foreign exchange on imported components — Currency fluctuations can raise procurement costs for imported components and hurt profitability. Exposures are monitored and procurement strategies are aligned to reduce the effect.
- Project execution on a large capex pipeline — Delays in capacity expansion or new projects (the compressor plant, the refrigerator plant, consolidation moves) could hurt planned operating and financial outcomes. The company mitigates through phased implementation and regular reviews.
- Economic and demand risk — Inflation, interest rates and changing consumer demand may affect performance and profitability. The company relies on a diversified product portfolio and broad customer base to offset this.
- Regulatory and product-standard changes — Evolving product standards and statutory requirements may force operational and product-level changes.
- Skilled talent availability and retention — Availability and retention of skilled talent may limit operational efficiency and expansion.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: PGEL provides end-to-end ODM and OEM manufacturing (product design and engineering, tooling, plastic moulding, sheet metal, PCB assembly and final assembly) for consumer-durable and electronics brands. Its product business is anchored by room air conditioners and washing machines, alongside air coolers, electronics (TV boards, AC controllers, CCTV camera solutions) and precision plastic moulding for automotive and sanitaryware customers; LED televisions are made through the Goodworth Electronics joint venture. It is entering refrigerator manufacturing with a plant under construction at Sri City, Andhra Pradesh.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Room Air Conditioners:** Split air conditioners, Window air conditioners, Indoor units, Outdoor units
- **Washing Machines:** Semi-automatic washing machines (6 kg to 20 kg), Fully automatic top-load washing machines (6 kg to 14 kg)
- **Air Coolers:** Desert air coolers, Personal air coolers, Window air coolers
- **Refrigerators (planned):** Direct Cool models, Side-by-Side models
- **LED Televisions (via JV Goodworth Electronics):** LED televisions 32 to 100 inches, Interactive Flat Panel Displays
- **Electronics:** PCB assemblies, Electronic control modules, Electronic sub-assemblies, TV boards, AC controllers, CCTV camera solutions
- **Plastic Moulding:** Injection moulded components for automotive, electronic equipment and sanitaryware, In-wall tank assemblies, Toilet seats, Plastic moulded refrigerator component kits
- **Tooling:** Injection moulds, Precision tools, Manufacturing tooling solutions

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin impacted by 250 bps in Q4 due to commodity inflation (copper, aluminum, plastics) and 20% rupee depreciation; price hikes of 10-12% implemented but partially offset by forex volatility; LPG crisis added exorbitant fuel switching costs; normalized margins expected to recover to historical averages in FY27 as pricing aligns and operating leverage returns.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: better than industry (FY27); margin: targeting 8% EBITDA margin (FY27); order inflow: robust in washing machines (30-35% growth expected); capex/commissioning: INR400cr FY27 capex; compressor facility (Supa) to commission Q4FY27; refrigerant plant (Sri City) to commission Q4FY27; washing machine expansion (Greater Noida) already operational.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Strong order visibility in washing machines; compressor and refrigerant facilities have anchor customer commitments; no specific order book value disclosed.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Compressor manufacturing (2M units, expandable to 4M) and refrigerant plant (Sri City) to unlock backward integration; washing machine capacity expansion; plastic molding consolidation at Salarpur to improve margins; SAP migration improving planning and inventory visibility.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Complete backward integration of room-AC manufacturing by building a rotary compressor plant at Supa; management calls the compressor the largest imported input in a room air conditioner and the last major piece of its backward-integration journey.
- Diversify beyond room air conditioners: scale up washing machines and enter refrigerators (Sri City plant, Phase 1 Direct Cool and Side-by-Side) as a new vertical.
- Consolidate manufacturing into fewer, larger, better-utilised facilities to cut overheads, including consolidating moulding operations on land acquired in Rajasthan and winding down the corresponding Greater Noida operations.
- Use the completed group-wide SAP migration for monthly plant- and product-line cost analysis and control to improve margins.
- Keep investing in R&D and new ODM product platforms across every category.
- Keep capex going through a soft season rather than slowing the long-term build-out.
- Optimise working capital as a key focus area in the coming quarters.
- Pursue openings in global supply chains created by new FTAs and government support for domestic manufacturing.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY 2025-26 PGEL ran its largest capex programme to date. The new washing machine facility at Greater Noida (1.8 million units annual capacity) became operational, and step-down subsidiary Next Generation Manufacturers' Bhiwadi AC unit became operational and contributed to production in Q4 FY 2025-26. Construction started on the refrigerator facility at Sri City, Andhra Pradesh (1.2 million units annual capacity; Phase 1 Direct Cool and Side-by-Side; production planned from FY 2026-27), on a 50-acre parcel where PGEL plans to invest around Rs 1,000 crore over the next 5 years. The rotary compressor facility at Supa (Phase 1 capacity 2 million units) is under construction, with equipment installation underway and mass production planned for Q4 FY 2026-27. Next Generation Manufacturers signed an MoU with the Government of Maharashtra for a Rs 1,000 crore greenfield project at Kamargaon, Ahilyanagar. The company is also consolidating its footprint: some Greater Noida units are moving to the Salarpur campus, and PG Technoplast has acquired land in Rajasthan to consolidate moulding operations, winding down the corresponding Greater Noida operations in due course.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Penetration of room air conditioners, washing machines and refrigerators remains very low among Indian households; rising incomes, urbanisation and nuclearisation of families support structural demand.
- In a difficult season brands consolidate their outsourcing with reliable partners; the RAC segment grew while the category declined.
- Industry channel inventories have normalised meaningfully, and the company enters FY2027 with new capacities coming on stream.
- FY2026 margins were hit by an early monsoon that shortened the cooling season, the mid-year GST rate revision, the transition to revised energy-efficiency norms, elevated input costs, inventory carrying and finance costs, and underutilised expanded capacities.
- Margin levers management names: granular cost control enabled by SAP, plant consolidation, better asset utilisation, and in-house compressors.
- Government encouragement of domestic manufacturing (PLI, ECMS, Make in India) and localisation support demand for Indian EMS and contract manufacturers.
- Washing-machine growth came from new Greater Noida capacity and market response to new product platforms.
- Robust order book across product categories provided strong business visibility (MD&A key highlights).
- Chairman: in the ODM business the strength of the product platforms is the strength of the order book.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: FY26 saw severe margin compression from 20% rupee depreciation, LPG-driven production shutdowns, and inventory gluts, but FY27 outlook is turning positive with normalized channel inventory, new capacity in compressors and refrigerants coming online, and margin recovery expected toward 8% EBITDA margin as operating leverage returns and cost discipline takes effect.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: PG Electroplast is an Indian electronics manufacturing services (ODM/OEM) partner that designs and builds room air conditioners, washing machines, air coolers and components for 70+ Indian and global brands.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: PGEL provides end-to-end ODM and OEM manufacturing (product design and engineering, tooling, plastic moulding, sheet metal, PCB assembly and final assembly) for consumer-durable and electronics brands. Its product business is anchored by room air conditioners and washing machines, alongside air coolers, electronics (TV boards, AC controllers, CCTV camera solutions) and precision plastic moulding for automotive and sanitaryware customers; LED televisions are made through the Goodworth Electronics joint venture. It is entering refrigerator manufacturing with a plant under construction at Sri City, Andhra Pradesh.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- PG Technoplast Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%), subsidiary since December 17, 2020; rents premises from PGEL at Supa (Ahmednagar) and Greater Noida; buys and sells goods, raw materials, capital goods and services with PGEL.
- Next Generation Manufacturers Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned step-down subsidiary (100%), since March 02, 2024.
- PG Plastronics Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%), since June 22, 2021; yet to commence operations; rents premises from PGEL at Greater Noida.
- Goodworth Electronics Private Limited — JV: 50% joint venture, associated July 31, 2023; rents premises from PGEL at Greater Noida; buys products from PGEL.
- Goodworth Innovations Private Limited — JV: Wholly owned subsidiary of the Goodworth joint venture (50% effective); not operational.
- Goodworth Gadgets Private Limited — JV: Wholly owned subsidiary of the Goodworth joint venture (50% effective); not operational.
- Goodworth Optima Private Limited — JV: Wholly owned subsidiary of the Goodworth joint venture (50% effective); not operational.
- Goodworth Appliances Private Limited — JV: Wholly owned subsidiary of the Goodworth joint venture (50% effective); not operational.
- Mr. Vishal Gupta — related party: Promoter and Director; leases the Roorkee factory (30-year lease deed dated 06/11/2009) and the registered office at Jasola, New Delhi to the company.
- M/s PG Electronics — related party: Firm in which a director is a partner; leases the Roorkee factory to the company under the 30-year lease deed dated 06/11/2009.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: RAC revenue: -12% YoY (Q4); +9% YoY (FY26); Washing machines: +70% YoY (Q4); +52% YoY (FY26); Coolers: -10.8% YoY (Q4); -8.2% YoY (FY26); Goodworth Electronics (JV): +44% YoY revenue (Q4); EBITDA improved to INR6.19cr from INR0.94cr (Q4).

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Room Air Conditioners:** Split air conditioners, Window air conditioners, Indoor units, Outdoor units
- **Washing Machines:** Semi-automatic washing machines (6 kg to 20 kg), Fully automatic top-load washing machines (6 kg to 14 kg)
- **Air Coolers:** Desert air coolers, Personal air coolers, Window air coolers
- **Refrigerators (planned):** Direct Cool models, Side-by-Side models
- **LED Televisions (via JV Goodworth Electronics):** LED televisions 32 to 100 inches, Interactive Flat Panel Displays
- **Electronics:** PCB assemblies, Electronic control modules, Electronic sub-assemblies, TV boards, AC controllers, CCTV camera solutions
- **Plastic Moulding:** Injection moulded components for automotive, electronic equipment and sanitaryware, In-wall tank assemblies, Toilet seats, Plastic moulded refrigerator component kits
- **Tooling:** Injection moulds, Precision tools, Manufacturing tooling solutions

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Consumer durables brands (room air conditioners, washing machines, air coolers, refrigerators)
- Consumer electronics (LED televisions, electronic modules)
- Automotive OEMs (engineered plastic components)
- Sanitaryware / bathroom fittings
- India (domestic brands) and global brands served from India

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Strong order visibility in washing machines; compressor and refrigerant facilities have anchor customer commitments; no specific order book value disclosed.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: better than industry (FY27); margin: targeting 8% EBITDA margin (FY27); order inflow: robust in washing machines (30-35% growth expected); capex/commissioning: INR400cr FY27 capex; compressor facility (Supa) to commission Q4FY27; refrigerant plant (Sri City) to commission Q4FY27; washing machine expansion (Greater Noida) already operational.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Compressor manufacturing (2M units, expandable to 4M) and refrigerant plant (Sri City) to unlock backward integration; washing machine capacity expansion; plastic molding consolidation at Salarpur to improve margins; SAP migration improving planning and inventory visibility.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Penetration of room air conditioners, washing machines and refrigerators remains very low among Indian households; rising incomes, urbanisation and nuclearisation of families support structural demand.
- In a difficult season brands consolidate their outsourcing with reliable partners; the RAC segment grew while the category declined.
- Industry channel inventories have normalised meaningfully, and the company enters FY2027 with new capacities coming on stream.
- FY2026 margins were hit by an early monsoon that shortened the cooling season, the mid-year GST rate revision, the transition to revised energy-efficiency norms, elevated input costs, inventory carrying and finance costs, and underutilised expanded capacities.
- Margin levers management names: granular cost control enabled by SAP, plant consolidation, better asset utilisation, and in-house compressors.
- Government encouragement of domestic manufacturing (PLI, ECMS, Make in India) and localisation support demand for Indian EMS and contract manufacturers.
- Washing-machine growth came from new Greater Noida capacity and market response to new product platforms.
- Robust order book across product categories provided strong business visibility (MD&A key highlights).
- Chairman: in the ODM business the strength of the product platforms is the strength of the order book.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin impacted by 250 bps in Q4 due to commodity inflation (copper, aluminum, plastics) and 20% rupee depreciation; price hikes of 10-12% implemented but partially offset by forex volatility; LPG crisis added exorbitant fuel switching costs; normalized margins expected to recover to historical averages in FY27 as pricing aligns and operating leverage returns.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing strategic capex: compressors, refrigerants, WM expansion; maintaining discipline on returns; no dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on cash flow generation and working capital normalization in FY27.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY 2025-26 PGEL ran its largest capex programme to date. The new washing machine facility at Greater Noida (1.8 million units annual capacity) became operational, and step-down subsidiary Next Generation Manufacturers' Bhiwadi AC unit became operational and contributed to production in Q4 FY 2025-26. Construction started on the refrigerator facility at Sri City, Andhra Pradesh (1.2 million units annual capacity; Phase 1 Direct Cool and Side-by-Side; production planned from FY 2026-27), on a 50-acre parcel where PGEL plans to invest around Rs 1,000 crore over the next 5 years. The rotary compressor facility at Supa (Phase 1 capacity 2 million units) is under construction, with equipment installation underway and mass production planned for Q4 FY 2026-27. Next Generation Manufacturers signed an MoU with the Government of Maharashtra for a Rs 1,000 crore greenfield project at Kamargaon, Ahilyanagar. The company is also consolidating its footprint: some Greater Noida units are moving to the Salarpur campus, and PG Technoplast has acquired land in Rajasthan to consolidate moulding operations, winding down the corresponding Greater Noida operations in due course.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledged severe FY26 headwinds but emphasized structural tailwinds (outsourcing trend, low AC penetration, energy transition); confident in new capacity execution and cost discipline; avoided giving FY27 guidance but signaled normalization and recovery.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- integration: room-AC components made in-house — evidence: at the Ahmednagar and Bhiwadi AC facilities 'plastic components, sheet metal components, cross flow fans, heat exchangers, copper tubing and controllers are all produced in-house' — against it: the rotary compressor is not yet in-house; the Supa compressor project is still in progress
- scale: room-AC manufacturing capacity — evidence: 4.5 million units RAC annual manufacturing capacity; company states it is the largest manufacturer of room AC CBUs in India — against it: the report attributes the FY 2025-26 operating-profit decline to negative operating leverage and lower capacity utilisation in the Room AC business
- technology: in-house ODM design platforms and tooling — evidence: tooling division established 2016; four ODM platforms for air conditioners launched in 2022 and a new ODM washing machine platform launched later
- integration: forward integration into refrigerators from its existing refrigerator component-kit supply — evidence: Sri City refrigerator facility under construction with 1.2 million units initial annual capacity planned [planned]

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: FX volatility (rupee at INR95.5 vs budgeted INR94); El Nino uncertainty impacting AC season; labor shortages due to fuel cost and new Labour Code; global geopolitical risks (Gulf conflict) disrupting LPG supply; margin recovery dependent on sustained price pass-through and stable exchange rates.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: LPG crisis caused 2-week shutdown in March, leading to INR300cr revenue loss; truck shortage stranded INR120cr of finished goods; forex loss of INR25.82cr in Q4 was largely due to mark-to-market on unhedged LCs at INR94.8; compressor facility requires no external approvals; 60% localization in compressors; inventory normalized from INR1,600cr (Mar) to target <INR900cr by June 2026.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Complete backward integration of room-AC manufacturing by building a rotary compressor plant at Supa; management calls the compressor the largest imported input in a room air conditioner and the last major piece of its backward-integration journey.
- Diversify beyond room air conditioners: scale up washing machines and enter refrigerators (Sri City plant, Phase 1 Direct Cool and Side-by-Side) as a new vertical.
- Consolidate manufacturing into fewer, larger, better-utilised facilities to cut overheads, including consolidating moulding operations on land acquired in Rajasthan and winding down the …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Subsidiary] "Our 100% subsidiary, PG Technoplast, reported INR 1,628.9 crores in revenue" in 1QFY27.
- [JV] "Our 50:50 JV, Goodworth Electronics, posted revenues of INR 177.3 crores in 1QFY27 vs. INR 147.5 crores in 1QFY26, with EBITDA of INR 6.3 crores vs. INR 4.3 crores YoY."
- [Milestone] "1QFY27 has been a strong growth period as consolidated quarterly revenues crossed INR 2,000 crores for the first time in the company's history."
- [Policy tailwinds] Industry outlook cites government reforms "such as Digital India, Make in India, Power for all and Jan Dhan-Aadhar-Mobile Trinity" and "the Government's initiatives of promoting electronic manufacturing and treating the industry as one of the key pillars of the Digital India Program".
